references.text: The same principle that one witness is not sufficient to condemn anyone to death, but multiple witnesses are required.
Reiterates the requirement of two or three witnesses to prove a case, and that one witness is not enough.
Jesus cites this principle of two or three witnesses in connection with church discipline.
Paul applies the principle of two or three witnesses when he warns the Corinthians.
Paul instructs Timothy not to accept an accusation against an elder without two or three witnesses.
Refers directly to the principle from the Mosaic Law that whoever rejects the law dies without mercy on the basis of two or three witnesses.
Jesus refers to the law concerning the credibility of two witnesses to confirm the truth about himself.
